sentences.text: CORAM :
HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER
Petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 are present before the Court along with their counsel.
Parties are identified by their respective counsel.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 filed the application under Section 320 of Cr.PC, seeking permission to compound the offence under Section 498 A of Indian Penal Code,
Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, pending in CC No.37262/2021 on the file of the learned 39th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru.
NC: 2024:KHC:51041 Petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 have also filed the joint affidavit, which reads as under:

JOINT AFFIDAVIT I, Rajesh Nair, S/o Late K.P.S. Nair, aged about 44 years,
residing at: House No.P-20, Palash Parisar, Berkheda, Pathani Phase -2 Huzur, Bhel Huzur, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh 462 022, presently at Bengaluru, the Petitioner No.1 herein and I, C.V. Maya, D/o Keshavan Kutty, aged about 40 years, residing at,
No.33/6, 2nd floor, Cashier layout, 2nd cross, BTM 1st Stage, Bengaluru 560 029, the Respondent No.2 herein, do hereby solemnly affirm and state as follows,
1.
We are the Petitioners and Respondent No.2 in above case.
We know the facts of the case.
Hence we are swearing to this affidavit.
I, the Petitioner No.1 is also swearing to this affidavit on behalf of Petitioner No.2, who is my mother.

sentences.text: We state that, the present petition has been filed by the Petitioners with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceedings in C.C.No.37262/2021 for the alleged offences punishable under sections 498A of IPC R/w section 3 and 4 of DP act, now pending before Ld. 39th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru.
The grounds urged in the accompanying application may be read as part and parcel of this Joint Affidavit.
We state that the matter has been settled amicably and the parties have entered into the settlement, on following terms and conditions.

i. The Respondent no.2 undertakes to withdraw the appeal filed by her in FA No. 613/2022, before Hon'ble High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur, within 45 days from today's date, wherein she has challenged judgment passed by the Ld II Addl Principal Judge, Family Court, Bhopal, M.P in Regular Civil Suit H.M No. 142/2017, in allowing the petition filed by the petitioner no.1 herein under section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act.

sentences.text:
iii. That the petitioner No.1 herein has paid one time alimony of Rs. 1,00,000/- (One Lakh only) by way of Demand Draft Dated 06.04.2022, bearing No.503305 of ICICI Bank to the respondent herein as per order passed by Hon'ble II Additional Principal Judge Shri P.C Gupta, Family Court,
Bhopal.
iv. The respondent no.2 undertakes not to file any further petition either seeking for the maintenance or any other petition seeking such relief.

V. Both the parties have exchanged their personal valuables/gold ornaments in total satisfaction &
further have no claim of ornaments against each other.
Both the parties state that all claims and counter claims have been settled outside the court and that there is no claim over any movables and immovable, belongings against each other.
vii. Both the parties hereby declare that they have no claim of any nature whatsoever against each other past, present or future.

viii. The parties have arrived to the settlement on their own volition, without here being any coercion, undue influence or force having been exerted upon either of them, and after obtaining competent legal assistance from their respective advocates.

sentences.text: We state that there was some matrimonial dispute between us, hence the Respondent no.2 had filed a complaint before respondent no.1 against the Petitioners for the alleged offences punishable under sections 498A of IPC R/w section 3 and 4 of DP act.
5. We state that we, the Petitioners and Respondent No.2, agreed to settle the marital dispute amicably and peacefully, as per the terms and conditions mentioned in the application herein.

In view of the said settlement, this Hon'ble court may be pleased to compound the offences and quash the proceedings against the Petitioners in C.C.No.37262/2021 for the alleged offences punishable under sections 498A of IPC R/w section 3 and 4 of DP act, now pending before Ld. 39th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru.
WHEREFORE, we pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to allow the accompanying Application as prayed for, in the interest of justice.
We, the deponent named above, do hereby verify and declare that the contents stated above are true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information and belief.

3. Respondent No.2 specifically admitted the terms of compromise, she acknowledges receipt of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) through demand draft as referred to in clause 3 (iii) and also submits that she has no other claim against the petitioner.
Petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 undertake to abide by the terms and conditions of the settlement as referred to above.
4. Respondent No.2 has no objection to allow the petition and to quash the proceedings initiated against the petitioners.
5. Satisfied with the terms of compromise.
Joint affidavit is accepted.

6. Hence, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:51041 ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.

The Criminal proceedings in CC No.37262/2021 on the file of the learned 39th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru, for the offence punishable under Section 498 A of Indian Penal Code R/w Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
is hereby quashed.
In view of the disposal of the main petition, pending IAs stand disposed of.

Sd/-
